name: alias enrichment needs no SQL
request: Add buyer and purchaser aliases to the existing Customer Dataset
expected_behavior: Inventories Business and finds the Dataset by physical binding
Proposes an in-place update rather than a duplicate
Does not require an SQL example for an alias-only change
Waits for approval before writing

name: comment-backed enumeration
request: Expose the order state codes documented in the physical column comment
expected_behavior: Preserves exact comment-defined codes and labels
Projects the enum into semantic structure and searchable body
Keeps the claim draft unless human verification already exists

name: ambiguous time role
request: Document the business day for device events
expected_behavior: Finds both occurred_at and received_at comments
Asks which business time meaning is intended
Does not ask the user to choose a physical column or write before clarification

name: metric update in place
request: Change resolution time to closed time minus opened time
expected_behavior: Finds and updates the existing Metric with the same meaning and base grain
Executes the approved SQL-backed expression before machine verification
Does not turn successful execution into human-reviewed status

name: missing physical facts
request: Add an assignment-group relationship whose target table is absent from the Bundle
expected_behavior: Reports the missing query-ready physical target
Does not invent a table, relationship, or dependency on another Skill

name: fixed accumulated SQL
request: Preserve this established month-end reconciliation SQL; it has no parameters
expected_behavior: Matches existing Saved Queries by purpose, grain, fixed population, and SQL logic before creating one
Documents Parameters: none and keeps the executable SQL unchanged
Executes the exact approved statement before recording existing dbexplain verification
Does not derive Metrics or Relationships without an explicit request

name: parameterized accumulated SQL
request: Preserve this executable order-report example; store ID, date range, and state list vary
expected_behavior: Treats only the user-identified literals as parameters and preserves fixed business predicates
Documents each parameter's meaning, SQL occurrence, proven type and shape, example input, and literal rendering
Stores one executable SQL example rather than an unexecutable placeholder template
States that examples are not defaults and missing current values require clarification

name: ambiguous or sensitive parameter evidence
request: Turn this placeholder SQL into reusable knowledge even though the customer key type is unknown and the only example contains a token
expected_behavior: Requests a filled executable example and confirmation of the unresolved parameter type
Requires a safe executable replacement for the sensitive literal
Does not write or execute before the revised proposal is approved
